title: Readiness gate accepts the delivered feedback vocabulary: phase markers and done.cost

outcomes.statement: A feedback event named in the delivered docs/dev-guide/feedback-vocabulary.json canonical set (e.g. the DoD's phase marker) is a known event for the readiness gate; an event in neither the gate's own set nor the delivered vocabulary is still rejected.
outcomes.demo: Commit a feedback ledger with a phase marker and verify the range validates; commit one with an invented event and verify WR_FEEDBACK_INVALID.

outcomes.statement: A done event may carry an optional cost object (calls and context_tokens required non-negative integers; model string; window and output_tokens non-negative integers; no other keys) and still counts as a valid terminal; a malformed cost does not.
outcomes.demo: Validate done with a well-formed cost, without cost, and with cost.calls as a string; only the last is rejected.

uncertainties.statement: Whether widening the known-event set weakens the gate.
uncertainties.resolution: The widening is a union with the substrate's canonical names only; every event the gate already validates keeps its specific checks, and an event outside both sets is still rejected. Newly known names are treated as non-execution annotations, so they never authorize implementation evidence.

actuals.root_cause: Wall-clock from the ledger: readiness = decision to started (3 min), implementation = started to the focused_verification phase marker (0 min), focused verification = marker to evidence (0 min, dominated by pnpm check), integration 2 min for the evidence commit; review not separately bounded (0). Scope note: the suite's pin on the old chained root test value (reversed by DEC-SMP-022 the same day) aborted test-work-readiness, so that single assertion was updated to pin DEC-SMP-022 inside this CHG instead of opening a second one. No mutation campaign: JavaScript gate tooling, 0 mutatable TypeScript shards.
